question.text: The amount of heat produced in an electric circuit depends upon the current $(I)$, resistance $(R)$ and time $(t)$. If the error made in the measurements of the above quantities are $2 \%, 1 \%$ and $1 \%$ respectively then the maximum possible error in the total heat produced will be

solution.text:
Given : $\frac{\Delta I}{I} \times 100=2 \%$;
$\frac{\Delta R}{R} \times 100=1 \%$ and $\frac{\Delta t}{t} \times 100=1 \%$
Heat produced, $H=I^2 R t$
Maximum possible error in heat produced,
$$
\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{\Delta H}{H} \times 100 \\
& =2\left(\frac{\Delta I}{I} \times 100\right)+\frac{\Delta R}{R} \times 100+\frac{\Delta t}{t} \times 100 \\
& =2 \times 2 \%+1 \%+1 \%=6 \%
\end{aligned}
$$
